sources.note: LDAPv3 protocol wire format: Bind name/authentication fields, Filter ASN.1 CHOICE with and/or/not/present, and the search-request structure that injection abuses.
The WebSocket Protocol: Section 10.2 Origin Considerations (SHOULD verify Origin, 403 on unacceptable), 10.5 client authentication, 10.6 wss/TLS, 10.7 input validation, masking rules.

HTTP Semantics Section 7.2 Host and :authority - host as application-level routing mechanism, cache-poisoning and interception-proxy risk, and the requirement to verify the connection targets a valid IP.
CSP 1.0, origin of the X-Frame-Options header. Superseded by CSP2 for frame-ancestors.

OpenLDAP Administrator's Guide security chapter: anonymous/unauthenticated/authenticated bind modes, disallow bind_anon not preventing anonymous access, TCP wrappers, interface binding vs IP firewall.
session.use_strict_mode and session adoption, uninitialized session IDs, use_only_cookies, trans_sid, sid_length/sid_bits_per_character.
hash_equals timing-attack-safe string comparison - the PHP control against token comparison oracles.
hmac.compare_digest() guidance: compare_digest() over == to reduce timing attack vulnerability when verifying an externally supplied digest.
secrets module - cryptographically strong generation for security tokens, token_urlsafe/token_hex, and the explicit preference over random module.
Cookie attributes including httponly, secure, samesite, partitioned; Morsel attribute handling.
http.server security warnings: not recommended for production, CGIHTTPRequestHandler not intended for untrusted clients.
WHATWG WebSockets Standard: handshake construction, Sec-WebSocket-Key nonce, fail on non-101 status, and the rationale that redirects are not followed to stop cross-host WebSocket redirection.

Content Security Policy Level 2: frame-ancestors Section 7.7 including no default-src fallback, removal of frame-ancestors from meta-delivered policies, MUST-be-ignored in meta, and the X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN top-level-only comparison.
Tomcat HTTP Filter: antiClickJackingEnabled / antiClickJackingOption and click-jacking protection semantics.
Tomcat WebSocket How-To: RFC 6455 support, JSR-356 Java WebSocket API, write/session-close/ABNORMAL close timeouts and idle-timeout session behaviour.
mod_headers: onsuccess vs always condition - headers added only on success responses are absent on error and internal-redirect responses, a real gap for protection headers.
StrictHostCheck directive (default OFF, server responds to any hostname) and ServerTokens product-only behaviour.
add_header applies only to enumerated success status codes unless 'always' is set, and the if-and-only-if inheritance rule for nested locations.
proxy_set_header Host $host example - how the Host value is forwarded upstream through a reverse proxy.
set_real_ip_from / real_ip_header - the trusted-hop allowlist that governs whether forwarding headers are honoured.
client_max_body_size: request body size limit, 413 on exceed, and size 0 disabling the check entirely.
subprocess Security Considerations: no implicit shell, shell=True responsibility, shlex.quote(), and the Windows batch-file shell caveat (gh-114539).
tempfile secure creation via mkstemp rules, random filenames for shared temp dirs, and TemporaryFile having no visible filesystem entry on Unix.
child_process.exec/execFile/spawn: execFile does not spawn a shell by default, shell option enables it, the explicit 'do not pass unsanitized user input' warnings, and the Windows .bat/.cmd caveat.
Node HTTP request/response header access including Cookie retrieval and header name/value semantics.
escapeshellarg: argument-level quoting for exec/system/backtick, Windows variant behaviour, and multibyte locale caveat.
shell_exec - executes a command via the shell and returns the full output as a string.
is_uploaded_file: verifies a file arrived via HTTP POST to prevent tricking the script into operating on files such as /etc/passwd.
Handling file uploads: do not trust the client MIME value, check type server-side, do not use the client filename without validation, derive a safe unique name from binary data, size-limit notes.

Docker daemon attack surface: root privileges, only trusted users should control the daemon, shared host directory / host-root container primitive, and extra caution when provisioning containers from a web API.
Pod Security Standards: Privileged defined by absence of restrictions, allows known privilege escalations, and host namespace sharing (hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC) must be disallowed.

Jinja sandbox: SecurityError on unsafe attribute access, 'the sandbox alone is not a solution for perfect security', resource-exhaustion and side-effect caveats, is_safe_attribute/unsafe()/ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment.
Twig templates: HTML escaping manual vs automatic (default html strategy), the autoescape tag, and the rule that untrusted-source variables must be escaped.
Twig API: SandboxExtension enforcing the sandbox security policy for evaluating untrusted code, and EscaperExtension raw filter behaviour.
string.Template: substitute vs safe_substitute, invalid placeholder ValueError, get_identifiers/is_valid (3.11), and the subclassable delimiter/idpattern - a common weak-template injection surface.
The WebSocket Security Model: threat model for WebSocket deployments and the security considerations that accompany RFC 6455.
Content Security Policy Level 3 - note the fetched .txt build did not contain the frame-ancestors prose; use the W3C CSP2 document instead for quotable frame-ancestors spans.
HTTP/1.1 Message Syntax and Routing - request line, field syntax and header parsing rules relevant to Host handling.
HTTP/1.1 Semantics and Methods - method and status definitions including redirect semantics.
HTTP State Management Mechanism - the normative cookie attribute and scope rules behind cookie-based session flag findings.
Alternate HTML rendering of RFC 6265; use only if the .txt build proves unfetchable for the gate.
NIST SP 800-63B digital identity guidelines - publisher page only (landing text, no quotable normative prose); use for registration, not citation.
Deprecated cgi module - CGI execution surface, relevant to command-injection chains through legacy handlers.
Node fs module - file read/write and temporary-name handling relevant to upload storage analysis.
Node path module - path normalisation semantics underlying upload filename and traversal checks.
pathlib - pure-path operations and the separation of path computation from filesystem access.
shlex.quote/quoting - POSIX shell quoting utility recommended for escaping in shell-invoking subprocess calls.
ElementTree parser surface - default parser behaviour relevant to external-entity handling assumptions.
popen(3) - the standard-library shell-invoking process creation call, a common command-injection primitive.
nsswitch.conf(5) - name-service switch configuration governing how LDAP is consulted for identity lookups.
sshd_config(5) - a canonical remote-service configuration reference for hardening-default reviews.
PostgreSQL CREATE INDEX - server-side index construction, relevant to SQL-injection and DoS-by-query chains.
Kubernetes Ingress - host-based routing rules where an unvalidated host header selects a backend.
Docker daemon access protection - the control that limits who may control the daemon.
Kubernetes Secrets - exposure and default-at-rest-protection guidance.
Istio security concepts - service-mesh identity and authorisation model.
OpenSSL EVP_EncryptInit - cryptographic initialisation surface relevant to weak-default reviews.
FIRST CVSS v3.1 specification - the normative scoring definition for triage and severity assignment of misconfiguration findings.
FIRST CVSS v3.0 specification - prior-version scoring definitions.
AWS ALB troubleshooting - host-header routing and listener behaviour on managed load balancers.
ALB listener configuration - listener rules and the conditions under which upgrade-capable traffic is forwarded.
Azure API Management WebSocket API - gateway-level WebSocket pass-through and policy behaviour.
python-ldap filter handling - RFC 4515 filter construction helpers. NOTE: builds on readthedocs.io, which the config treats as a builder host and filters out of publisher counting.
Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol (HTCPCP/1.0) - an obsolete protocol specification; recorded so future waves do not re-probe it as a candidate.
Address Allocation for Private Internets - already cited in db/sources.json; do not reuse.
